chunks: And among what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated, from Muʿāwiyah ibn Ḥukaym, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād Dhī al-Nāb, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who prayed Maghrib, then did not know whether he had prayed two or three. He said: He recites the tashahhud and concludes, then he stands and prays one rakʿah. If he had prayed three, then this would be a supererogatory prayer; and if he had prayed two, then this would complete the salat.

And this, by Allah, is among that which can never be established for me. So the proper approach regarding these two reports is that the earlier reports are not to be opposed by them, because their source is one and the same, namely ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, and he is weak and corrupt in doctrine; what is exclusively reported by him is not acted upon. The sect has agreed to abandon acting upon this report. It is also possible that the intended meaning in these two reports concerns one who became forgetful in the supererogatory Maghrib prayer, in which case it is permissible for him to build upon what the report contains and complete what remains. It is also possible that it is to be understood regarding one whose assumption inclines strongly to that, and even if he is not certain, it is permissible for him to build upon the greater number, while the addition of the rakʿah mentioned therein is taken as a recommendation.

key_terms.تَطَوُّعًا: a supererogatory or voluntary prayer act
key_terms.ضَعِيفٌ: weak in reliability as a transmitter
key_terms.يَتَشَهَّدُ: he recites the tashahhud before concluding the prayer

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in Shia hadith for doubting between two and three rakʿahs in Maghrib prayer?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling for one who doubts, in Maghrib prayer, whether he has prayed two rakʿahs or three. It then states that this particular report is not relied upon against other reports because its basis goes back to ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, and possible alternative interpretations are offered for reconciling it.
